types.name: PING_SERVER
types.description: Connection and command-path probe. No game state change, no domain event. Introduced by p0-01-bootstrap; p0-02 sends it over the realtime connection to measure the command round trip through the tick loop.

types.name: PING_REPLY
types.description: Type-specific answer to an ACCEPTED PING_SERVER, produced in the tick that handled it. Always arrives after that command's COMMAND_RESULT.

types.name: COMMAND_RESULT
types.description: Adjudication result of one command: ACCEPTED (taken into the simulation on the envelope tick) or REJECTED with a reason code. Accepted is not completed. Introduced by p0-02-networking-spike; p1-01-ship-movement adds the RATE_LIMITED and STALE_INPUT reason codes, compatible value additions at the same schema_version. p1-02-mining adds TARGET_UNKNOWN, COOLDOWN_ACTIVE, TARGET_OUT_OF_RANGE, SHIP_TOO_FAST, RESOURCE_DEPLETED, RECORDING_BACKLOG and CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, again a compatible value addition at the same schema_version.

types.name: SESSION_READY
types.description: First message on an authenticated realtime connection: session_id, world_id, the actor_id the server decided, tick_hz and the server build. Introduced by p0-02-networking-spike.

types.name: SESSION_OPENED
types.description: An authenticated actor became present in the world. Persisted to domain_events. Importance level 0 by design - it does not become a Historical Event. 'history' joins consumers when the history crate exists (p2). Introduced by p0-02-networking-spike.

types.name: SESSION_CLOSED
types.description: The presence interval opened by SESSION_OPENED ended, with the reason. Shares the opening event's correlation_id. Persisted to domain_events. Introduced by p0-02-networking-spike.

types.name: SET_SHIP_CONTROL
types.description: One tick of control intent (thrust and turn) for the ship the session's actor is flying. Carries no position, velocity or orientation: the client cannot describe where its ship is, only what it is trying to do (principle 1, I-26). The server consumes at most one input per tick per session, so sending faster buys no extra movement. Introduced by p1-01-ship-movement.

types.name: WORLD_SNAPSHOT
types.description: Full authoritative state of every ship at one tick, plus the newest input_seq the server consumed for the receiving session. The only way any client learns a position, its own included. Introduced by p1-01-ship-movement.

types.name: SHIP_SPAWNED
types.description: A ship entity started existing at a position. Distinct from SESSION_OPENED, which is about the actor (GDD section 4). Caused by the SESSION_OPENED of the same tick: the first contract in the project where causation_id is non-null. Importance level 0 by design. 'history' joins consumers when the history crate exists (p2). Introduced by p1-01-ship-movement.

types.name: SHIP_DESPAWNED
types.description: The ship entity stopped existing, with the reason and its last position. Caused by the SESSION_CLOSED that started its linger window - possibly many ticks earlier, and not necessarily from the session that spawned the ship. A pilot disconnecting does not despawn a ship. causation_id never equals event_id. Importance level 0 by design. Introduced by p1-01-ship-movement.

types.name: SHIP_CLASS
types.description: Shape of a ship class file such as data/ships/scout-s01.json. The designer owns the values; this contract owns the fields and the ranges outside which a value is a broken simulation rather than a balance choice. Every movement field feeds the ADR-0010 integrator on both the server and the client's prediction of it. producers is empty: the table is hand-authored, not emitted by any component. Introduced by p1-01-ship-movement.

types.name: STAR_SYSTEM
types.description: Shape of a star system file such as data/world/systems/cradle.json: coordinate space, soft and hard boundary, deterministic spawn ring, ship linger and reconnect window, and client-only reference markers. hard_boundary_radius_m has a hard ceiling that comes from the float32 rendering budget (ADR-0009), not from design. Introduced by p1-01-ship-movement.

types.name: SYNC_TUNING
types.description: Shape of data/movement/sync-tuning.json: the networking values that are FELT - snapshot rate, input pacing, remote interpolation delay and the reconciliation thresholds - kept out of code literals so that tuning never means editing Rust or C#. Deliberately excludes tick_hz (a world constant, I-19), the quantisation scales (ADR-0009) and the integrator identity (ADR-0010): those are laws, not tunables. Introduced by p1-01-ship-movement.

types.name: MINE_RESOURCE
types.description: Intent to perform one extraction at a deposit. The payload is the deposit id and nothing else: no quantity, mineral, position or distance (principle 1, spec p1-02 I-48). The first state-changing command of the project: command_id is a durable idempotency key across sessions, reconnects and restarts (ADR-0013 section 3). Introduced by p1-02-mining.

types.name: MINERAL_MINED
types.description: One accepted extraction, written in the same transaction as the inventory, deposit and processed_commands rows (ADR-0013). The only explanation an inventory quantity has. causation_id is the MINE_RESOURCE command_id - the first command-caused event. Importance level 0: NOT historical by itself; the history runner turns only the first one per (world, star system, mineral) into MINERAL_DISCOVERED (ADR-0014). Introduced by p1-02-mining.

types.name: MINERAL_DISCOVERED
types.description: The first Historical Event type of the project (HSE section 89 #1), Level 2 Regional, rule mineral-discovery@1: the smallest-(tick, sequence) MINERAL_MINED of a (world, star system, mineral). At most one per key; deterministic UUIDv5 id. Reaches clients only inside HISTORICAL_EVENT_NOTICE. Introduced by p1-02-mining.

types.name: INVENTORY_STATE
types.description: The receiving actor's full inventory: after SESSION_READY and in every tick it changed (after the COMMAND_RESULT of an accepted MINE_RESOURCE). The client never computes inventory (spec p1-02 I-49). Introduced by p1-02-mining.

types.name: DEPOSIT_FIELD_STATE
types.description: Dynamic state of every deposit of the star system, broadcast after SESSION_READY and in every tick a deposit's visible state changed. An unrevealed deposit carries null mineral, reserve, remainder and reveal tick so nothing leaks before the first extraction (spec p1-02 I-68). Introduced by p1-02-mining.

types.name: HISTORICAL_EVENT_NOTICE
types.description: One historical record for a player: LIVE after the history runner commits it, BACKFILL for every existing visible record when a session opens. Never before commit. The history runner produces the record (MINERAL_DISCOVERED); the tick driver/gateway wraps it into this message - envelope tick, message_id and delivery are known only there (ADR-0014 section 6, T0 agreement). Producer is therefore server. Introduced by p1-02-mining.

types.name: MINERAL
types.description: Shape of data/minerals/{id}.json: display name, rarity (presentation only), yield per extraction and regeneration, integer kilograms. Introduced by p1-02-mining.

types.name: DEPOSIT_FIELD
types.description: Shape of data/world/deposits/{star_system_id}.json: deposit positions, radii and names (read by both) plus mineral and initial reserve (server-side truth; the client must not read them from its copy - DEPOSIT_FIELD_STATE is the only way they reach a player). Introduced by p1-02-mining.

types.name: MINING_RULES
types.description: Shape of data/mining/mining-rules.json: range from deposit surface, maximum ship speed and cooldown. The server judges with them; the client only displays whether they are met. Introduced by p1-02-mining.

types.name: SIGNIFICANCE_RULE
types.description: Shape of one history rule file, data/history/rules/{rule_id}.json: rule identity, rule_version and output constants (level, visibility, evidence). The condition is Rust code. A golden test binds rule_version to this file's content (ADR-0014 section 5). Introduced by p1-02-mining.
